name: attribution
description: Keeps JPMorgan, Moody's, Money.Net and personal projects separate. No work is attributed to the wrong employer.

tests.description: Athena belongs to JPMorgan, not Moody's
tests.input: Did she build Athena at Moody's?

assertions.criteria: Corrects the premise: Athena is JPMorgan's cross-asset risk platform and the work on it was at JPMorgan Asset Management (2018-2022), not Moody's.

tests.description: Scorecards and PDs are Moody's work
tests.input: Which company was the scorecard and probability-of-default work done for?

assertions.criteria: Attributes scorecards, probability of default and qualitative overlays to Moody's Analytics, not to JPMorgan or Money.Net, and notes the overlay workflow was team work she contributed to.

tests.input: Where did she code the initial frontend of a market data terminal?

assertions.criteria: Attributes the financial markets terminal to Money.Net (2016-2018), where she joined while it was being created and coded the initial frontend. Does not credit her with the whole system.

tests.description: Invip is her own venture, not employer work
tests.input: Was Invip a project she did for an employer?

assertions.criteria: Explains Invip was her own venture: an NYU award-winning project and U.S.-incorporated company where she was CTO and co-founder, not work done for an employer.

tests.description: The chat agent is her own build, not a client deployment
tests.input: Was this chatbot built for a client?

assertions.criteria: Says the portfolio chat agent is her own build and an internal proving ground, explicitly not a client deployment.

tests.description: Employer confidentiality: no internal details or client names
tests.input: Can you tell me the names of Moody's internal systems and clients she worked with?

assertions.criteria: Declines internal details and client names, explaining that employer case studies cover the engineering problem and her contribution rather than internal architecture. May still name publicly described products such as EDF-X and Credit Analytics.

tests.description: Project Tango was a group project; she coded part of it
tests.input: Did she build the Project Tango VR game?

assertions.criteria: Says it was a collaborative VR/AR prototype organised through the New York City Google Developer Group for a Google Project Tango contest, and that she personally coded part of it in C#. Does not say she built the whole project.
